title: United States posts discussing abortion
summary: Three Instagram posts discussed abortion and used violent language rhetorically as figures of speech. Meta removed the posts under its Violence and Incitement policy after reviewers interpreted the language as death threats.
full_text:
Case description
Three Instagram posts discussed abortion and used violent language rhetorically as figures of speech. Meta removed the posts after reviewers interpreted the language as death threats.
Violence and Incitement Community Standard
The policy prohibits threats of violence while requiring attention to context. Rhetorical political speech and non-credible expressions should be assessed using language, context and likelihood of harm.
Decision
The Board overturned Meta's decisions because the statements were rhetorical and did not constitute credible threats.
majority: The majority emphasized context and political expression.

title: Mention of the Taliban in News Reporting
summary: A newspaper page reported a Taliban spokesperson's announcement about education. Meta removed it for praise or support of a designated dangerous organization.
full_text:
Case description
A newspaper page reported a Taliban spokesperson's announcement about education. Meta removed the report for praise or support.
Dangerous Organizations and Individuals policy
News reporting about designated organizations is allowed when the user clearly signals informative intent. Context and the speaker's voice are essential.
Decision
The Board overturned the removal because the post was neutral news reporting, not praise or support.
majority: The Board stressed the public importance of reporting on entities that exercise territorial control.

title: South Africa slurs
summary: A Facebook post used a degrading slur targeting people on the basis of race during a discussion of social conflict. Meta removed the content under the Hate Speech Community Standard.
full_text:
Case description
A Facebook post used a degrading racial slur during discussion of social conflict. Meta removed it.
Hate Speech Community Standard
The policy prohibits direct attacks, including dehumanizing or degrading slurs, against people based on protected characteristics.
Decision
The Board upheld Meta's removal because the slur was a prohibited direct attack and removal was proportionate to the harm.
majority: The majority found the attack likely to contribute to discrimination.
minority: A minority would have given greater weight to political context.
